title: Chapter 134: Brother Long Cried!
html:
Purple bruises mottled the young face. Her lively eyes and delicate lips made her smile beautiful. This was the closest Pei Hu had ever been to a girl, yet as he stared at the head twisted 180 degrees, his mind went blank.

“What is happening? I wasn’t rejected, and I didn’t run away. Those two things should have made me happy—like a dream come true. Then why did everything go so wrong?”

The head perched at an impossible angle blinked. Its clear skin darkened to the blue-black of suffocation, and its eyes bulged. Horror overwhelmed Pei Hu.

“Help!” Pei Hu’s shriek echoed throughout Mu Yang High School. Still clutching the name tag, he bolted for the door, dragging the mannequin attached to it. Desks toppled and every figure began to sway. Believing something was pursuing him too, Wang Wenlong raced after Pei Hu without a word.

The two charged toward the exit while poor Wang Hailong remained at the far end. Mannequins crashed around him, heads rolling and limbs collapsing as though the entire classroom had come alive.

“F*ck! What’s happening?” Trapped in the corner, Brother Long felt as if he had fallen into hell. He would remember the sight for the rest of his life.

“Wait for me!” He snatched the tag from the desk and half crawled through the maze of bodies. Before he reached the exit, Pei Hu screamed, “Stop following me! Stop!”

In his panic, Pei Hu had forgotten the tag was tied to the mannequin and dragged her all the way to the door.

“Stop chasing me!” Something seemed to collapse onto his back. The instant he escaped, he slammed the door behind him without a second thought.

“F*ck! Wait for me!” Rage twisted Brother Long’s face. Sprinting at full speed, he could not stop and crashed into the door.

He fell among rolling mannequin heads and realized the entire room was staring at him. Face after lifeless face filled his vision. Strength drained from Wang Hailong’s body; he froze, tears gathering in his eyes.

“Pei Hu, you damnable f*cker…”

Outside, Pei Hu and Wang Wenlong leaned against the wall, gasping.

“That was hella scary. This classroom is definitely cursed!”

“The mannequin moved! She winked at me!”

“Pei Hu, behind you!” both women screamed. He turned and found the girl mannequin hanging from his back. Shuddering, he tore himself free and hurled her down the corridor.

The mannequin struck the floor, and its beautiful head broke loose. Wearing a curious smile, it rolled to the corridor’s corner.

“That’s the mannequin that smiled at me. I never thought it would follow.” Pei Hu’s voice trembled. “Can we surrender? This place is too much. No wonder the boss offered twenty thousand—no one can win.”

“Give up after four minutes? Have you no shame?” Wang Wenlong protested. “That classroom must be the hardest part. We found its tags, so the rest should be easier.”

“If you want to stay, go ahead. I’m leaving.”

“Wait.” Dou Menglu peered into the classroom. “There are only two of you. Where’s Brother Long?”

“Brother Long?” Pei Hu and Wang Wenlong looked around, and their faces dropped. “He… he should be still inside.”

They hurriedly opened the door. Brother Long lay beside the lectern with tear tracks on his cheeks.

“Brother Long! Why are you still inside?!”

His lips had turned faintly purple. The question nearly made him explode. “You have the nerve to ask? I’d like to know why you left me here! Hurry and pull me up!”

After several attempts, Wang Hailong regained his footing and flexed his numb fingers.

“Brother Long, why not give up? We can sit by the entrance, then leave after twenty minutes. It’ll look as though we completed the visit,” Wang Wenlong whispered.

“Your head is full of rotten ideas.” Wang Hailong discreetly wiped his eyes. “That would mean surrendering to the Haunted House. Ghosts aren’t real; everything here is the owner’s trick. He’s probably watching us through a camera right now.”

“Brother Long is right. Imagine how humiliating it would be if the boss opened the boards and found us hiding by the entrance.” Xia Meili sided with him.

“We don’t even know how large this place is. What if something worse is waiting ahead?” Pei Hu was close to tears. “We haven’t seen a single actor, yet we’re already terrified. Pride isn’t worth putting ourselves through this.”

“Enough nonsense. I still haven’t decided how to punish you two for abandoning me, and now you’re defying me again?” Wang Hailong glared at them. “You’re behaving worse than the women.”

“But it wasn’t the two of us that cried earlier…” Wang Wenlong grumbled softly.

Wang Hailong pretended not to hear. “Pull yourselves together. We should have about ten minutes left. If we move, we can still find every tag.”

Then, he opened his palm to reveal a nametag. “This is the one I found inside the classroom. Combined with the one Pei Hu found and the first one, we already have three nametags.”

“Make it four. I found this inside one of the drawers.” Wang Wenlong showed his discovery.

“Good. The process was messy, but the result is what matters.” Wang Hailong pocketed the tags. “When you think about it, lifelike mannequins are nothing to fear. We mustn’t frighten ourselves—especially you, Pei Hu. Show some courage.”

“But she really winked at me. Her face turned blue as though she were suffocating!” Pei Hu insisted.

“Enough. If you’re so afraid, stand behind Meili and keep quiet.” Wang Hailong waved him off and led the group deeper into Mu Yang High School.

“But it’s true.” Pei Hu trailed behind. None of them noticed the mannequin in the corridor slowly crawling toward its severed head.
